About Fairphone

Fairphone is more than just a company; we are a global leader in sustainable, modular electronics, on a mission to change the electronics industry from the inside out. Built on strong social and environmental values, we are a diverse and inclusive team from all walks of life creating market consumer electronics that make a real impact.

At Fairphone, you will find a supportive and safe space where everyone can be themselves, collaborate openly, and have the freedom to learn and grow because that's how we innovate and drive change together!

So... are you a proactive, self-motivated team player who loves taking initiative and bringing positive energy? Do you thrive in a fast-moving start-up or scale-up environment? Are you a great communicator who values collaboration and embraces different perspectives? And most importantly, do you feel a strong connection to Fairphone's mission and values? If you're nodding along and thinking, "Yes, that's me!", then check out our vacancy below!

Please know that we acknowledge that we are living in a time where the use of AI can bring many efficiencies and support. However, we want to know the real YOU. Please try to limit the use of AI tools to generate answers to the application; we value authenticity and encourage you to use your creativity!

Location: Amsterdam (you must have the right to work in the Netherlands)
Hours: 32–40 hours per week
Start: 1st of the month
Contract duration: 1st 12-month employment contract with the possibility of extension to permanent
Deadline to apply: Rolling basis. Please apply as soon as possible.

About Your Role

As our QA Automation Engineer , you will shape and elevate the quality culture across our web development team. Reporting to the Lead Developer, you will sit at the intersection of technical automation, release management, and critical analysis across our two Agile Scrum development teams.

This is not a traditional downstream testing role. You will shift quality "left" by critically questioning requirements, spotting edge cases, and embedding acceptance criteria into Jira tickets before a single line of code is written. Today, much of our QA work is handled manually by our UX Designers and Implementation Manager. You will lead our transition into a modern, automated QA environment while retaining the pragmatic mindset needed to manage structured manual test plans for ongoing deployments and, around 1–2 major launches a year.

You will establish our automated pre-deploy gates, create scheduled bug-detection scripts, and define clear severity rules. You need to empower our developers to take true ownership of their own unit and integration tests, serving as the authority who makes the final go/no-go call on deployments.

Key Responsibilities & Objectives

Your Key Responsibilities

Automation Architecture & Ownership: Plan, build, and maintain our end-to-end test automation suites using Playwright with Python.
CI/CD Quality Gates: Integrate automated testing into GitHub Actions to create automated pre-deployment quality gates and run weekly automated bug-detection scripts across our webshop.
Refinement & Critical Analysis: Partner with Product Owners and UX Designers during Jira refinement sessions to define rigorous acceptance criteria, edge-case scenarios, as well as non-functional requirements.
Release & Bug Governance: Establish bug severity rules, manage staging environment improvements, and hold ultimate accountability for the go/no-go release decisions.
Manual Release Planning: Design and execute structured manual test plans, ensuring cross-device and -browser compatibility, usability, and performance. For frontend as well as for APIs and backend.
Enforce Quality Standards & Developer Accountability: Establish firm quality guardrails and hold developers accountable for their code's baseline quality. You will persistently challenge user stories, pull requests, and test coverage to ensure teams strictly adhere to quality rules before any increment moves to production.
Process Advice: Provide active input on refining our team's Definition of Done and improving our staging environment infrastructure alongside the Lead Developer and Product Owners.

Key Objectives

Build the Automation Foundation: Establish an automated CI/CD pre-deploy quality gate in GitHub Actions using Playwright (Python bindings) to safeguard our storefront and backend logic.
Embed Shift-Left Quality: Actively participate in Jira refinements, applying extreme critical thinking to identify technical edge cases and acceptance criteria before development begins.
Guide the QA Transition: Balance immediate needs (~30% manual test planning & release strategy) with long-term goals (~70% test automation setup and developer coaching).
Elevate Increment Quality: Take ownership of improving the overall quality of software increments shipped to production, driving a continuous reduction in post-release bugs and regression defects.

Your Skills & Experience

Minimum 3+ years of experience in Software Quality Assurance with a focus on web application test automation.
Hands-on experience setting up automation frameworks from scratch using Playwright (Python bindings preferred) or Cypress.
Practical experience configuring automated quality pipelines within CI/CD workflows using GitHub Actions.
Experience with, or an eagerness to explore and adopt, AI-assisted testing and development tools (e.g., GitHub Copilot, AI test generation tools) to accelerate test coverage, script maintenance, and bug detection.
Strong background in Agile Scrum environments, with proven success driving critical thinking, edge-case discovery, and acceptance criteria writing during user story refinement.
Solid understanding of web architectures and e-commerce platforms (experience with Python-based backends or platforms like Odoo is an advantage).
Ability to balance automated suite development with hands-on manual test strategy for major commercial releases.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; comfortable handling various projects at the same time, coaching team members and driving process improvements.

What Fairphone can offer you?

The opportunity to create an impact on the electronics industry around the world.
A diverse work environment full of international, passionate, warm-hearted team members.
25 paid holidays per year (based on a full-time contract) next to the other public holidays in the Netherlands. You’ll also get a day off on your birthday! Additionally, the longer you stay, the more holidays you get! 
Daily, healthy lunch, organic FairChain coffee, and many more tasty things.
You will join Fairphone’s collective pension scheme, and we will contribute to building your pension.
You will receive a MacBook, Fairbuds, and a Fairphone as working devices.
Hybrid working model: We are remote-friendly and also contribute up to €250 toward your home office set-up.
Public transport allowance – we fully cover your 2nd-class commute from your home to the office
Bike allowance – We support you with a bike purchase of up to €300, and you’ll also have a yearly repair budget of up to €100! We also cover 23 cents per km for your biking distance from home to the office (or train station) and back!
Grow with us! We encourage you to develop at Fairphone. In addition to €500 for L&D, we’ll support your career goals with coaching (Inuka), workshops, or courses that you can join with your development budget. You will get access to Udemy with unlimited courses and trainings.
Kitchen with beautiful views to the IJ waterfront.
There’s a gym in the building where you can build healthy habits, stay active and have fun with your colleagues, as well as a subscription to our mental & physical well-being services (Inuka & Urban Sports)

interne baan in regio Woerden
salaris tot 6000 euro bruto per maand
hybride werken + flexibel starten = veel vrijheid

Qua testen sta je er niet alleen voor want hier werkt ook nog een andere Test Engineer, iemand met enkele jaren ervaring. About Beyond Sports

Beyond Sports was founded in Alkmaar in 2014. We turn live player-tracking data into real-time 3D visualisations, so every position, sprint and pass becomes a virtual version of the match that can be broadcast, streamed or explored.

Our Emmy-winning technology has powered some of sport’s most talked-about broadcasts. These include NFL games reimagined as animated worlds and NHL games played out in blocky, game-style environments. Our clients include the NFL, NHL, NBA, Premier League and more.

Since 2022 we’ve been part of Sony Sports Technology, You’ll get the energy and ownership of a close-knit studio, backed by the reach and resources of one of the biggest names in entertainment. Our engine works on every screen, from traditional TV to mixed-reality headsets, so your work could reach fans wherever they watch.

Who We’re Looking For

We’re on the lookout for the next generation of engineers and product designers specialising in the following areas. From week one you’ll work alongside experienced engineers and designers on products used across the sports industry, owning real work in your discipline.

Mobile development: shipping matchday features for fans on Android and iOS.
Backend: building the services and data pipelines that keep live sports information flowing without a hitch.
Frontend: turning designs into fast, accessible interfaces that bring live sport to the browser.
Machine learning: cleaning and modelling sporting data, then turning it into predictions clients rely on.
QA: owning quality across our platforms, from test plans to automation that catches issues before fans do.
Product design: researching how fans and clients use our products, and designing what comes next.
Art, Unity and Unreal Engine development: creating virtual environments for live sports broadcasting.

When you apply, you’ll tell us which of these areas you want to work in, so we can match you with the right team.

What We Value

We’re all about high performance, in our products and in our people. We expect a lot, and we invest a lot in return, with real mentorship from the engineers and designers behind Emmy-winning broadcasts. Our team thrives on curiosity, ownership and helping each other get better.

We’re an office-first team working across time zones. Whether you join us in the Netherlands or Hungary, you’ll be part of a wider group that collaborates every day.

What Strong Candidates Bring

We hire for ability, not just credentials. Show us what you’ve built. Strong candidates typically bring:

An excellent degree, bootcamp or standout project experience in their chosen discipline
Deep curiosity about how things work, and the confidence to figure things out
Evidence of shipping things: apps, projects, portfolios, open-source contributions
Strong communication skills, because you’ll work closely with engineers, designers and product teams from day one
Comfort with ambiguity, and the drive to learn quickly with the support around you
An interest in sport and how technology changes the way fans experience it (a bonus, not essential)

Start date: September 2027

Location: Alkmaar, Netherlands (HQ) or Budapest, Hungary

Sound interesting? We’d love to hear from you. Applications close on Monday, 7 December 2026.

About The Assignment

Background 

At Thales, a project is currently ongoing to migrate away from the currently used Maven build system to Bazel for increased build performance, more granular caching, better parallelism and more deterministic artifacts. The current work for the Bazel migration project mainly consists of adopting or creating Bazel variants of the tools used within the different departments to build software components, systems and applications. One of these tools called Cucumber is used to run behavior driven integration tests. This is used to run containerized integration tests of software components using Podman containers in an environment similar to an actual deployment environment.

One of the advantages of Bazel is its highly efficient parallel execution of so-called actions, which include tests. However, this is currently conflicting with the limits of our integration test setup, mainly due to the limitations of Podman being single-threaded and non-reentrant which is at best unreliable when run in parallel, or will simply fail. This requires that parallel execution is disabled for these tests, significantly increasing build time and reducing part of the advantage that Bazel provides.

Assignment 

It needs to be investigated what options are available within the closed Thales environment to fully parallelize containerized integration tests when using Bazel as the build system, Podman as the container orchestrator and Cucumber as the integration testing framework.

The goal for this assignment is to create a proof-of-concept of an improved testing infrastructure capable of running containerized integration tests in parallel. The PoC needs to adhere to the following:

Support Bazel as the build system (working with Maven is a nice to have)

Uses Podman as the container orchestrator

Uses the current testing infrastructure as a base

Uses Cucumber as the integration testing framework

No tests shall require the ‘exclusive’ flag, which forces given tests to run sequentially.

Ideally, no test shall require the ‘flaky’ flag, which executes a test ‘n’ number of times, where the test is considered as passed so long as one of the attempts passes. Since this is also highly dependent on the tests themselves, this is not a hard requirement.
